newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SACCHI QUITS AS ITALY COACH, JOINS MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SACCHI QUITS AS ITALY COACH, JOINS MILAN.

text.p: Arrigo Sacchi has resigned as trainer of Italy's national soccer team and has joined AC Milan as its new coach, Italian television reported on Monday.

It quoted the spokesman for the Italian soccer federation, Antonello Valentini, as saying Sacchi had informed the federation of his decision, ending months of speculation about his future with the national side.
Italian soccer federation officials were not immediately available for comment on the report.

Sacchi's job with the national side has been in doubt since Italy slumped out of the European championship finals in England in the first round last June. His contract had been due to run until just before the World Cup finals in France in 1998.
At Milan, he would take over from Uruguayan Oscar Washington Tabarez, who joined the club this season on a one-year contract.
Milan, where Sacchi has had success as a trainer before, have had a black season so far and lost 3-2 away to Piacenza on Sunday. They are ninth in the serie A league.
